name: Receive and accession hospital referrals
sector: health care: medical laboratory testing and health services
summary: Hospital laboratories send the company specimens for specialised tests they do not perform themselves, packed in courier boxes with a manifest or an electronic order over a hospital LIS interface. At the reference laboratory, lab assistants check each box against its manifest, match each tube to its order, enter paper requisitions, check acceptability against each test's stability and specimen rules, label and aliquot, and route specimens to the reference benches, molecular pathology or send-out. Missing manifests, interface orders that never arrived, hospital test descriptions that do not map to the reference menu, and mismatched or unsuitable specimens cause holds and phone calls to the hospital, which make up most of the delay and coordinator effort.

baseline.org_archetype: The reference laboratory of a large Canadian community laboratory company that tests specialised assays for more than 500 hospitals, with about 70 percent of referrals ordered over bi-directional hospital LIS interfaces.
baseline.notes: LIS with HL7 order interfaces for larger hospitals; printed manifests and requisitions for the rest; nonconformances logged in the quality management system.

trigger: A courier or overnight shipment containing the requisition's specimens and manifest arrives at reference receiving.
end_state: The specimen is accessioned and at its reference bench, in the molecular pathology queue or on the send-out bench, or its tests are rejected and the hospital informed.

volume.seasonality: Weekday peaks with line hauls arriving in the afternoon and evening; lower on weekends and holidays.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's d_hospital_referrals driver: more than 500 hospitals served (dyn_hospital) at about 100 referred requisitions per hospital a month.

roles.title: Laboratory assistant, referral accessioning and send-outs

evidence.note: Referral receiving and accessioning by laboratory assistants; FTE 15, all that is left of the 25 in the role after the reference testing workflow claims 10; hands-on time implies more (see assumptions). Wage from Job Bank 33101 times 1.35 (jb33101); Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

Hospital client services coordinators resolve missing manifests, interface orders that did not arrive and specimen discrepancies with hospital laboratories; 5 of the 14 coordinators, the rest serve result delivery and send-outs. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

Charge technologists decide on specimens that fail acceptance; share of the 3 FTE left after reference testing. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Interface engine for HL7 orders and results with EMRs and hospital LIS
Courier routing, dispatch and web-based order and tracking system
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)
CRM for client accounts, sales pipeline and service cases
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording

steps.name: Receive the referral box at reference receiving
steps.description: A lab assistant signs for the courier tote or overnight box from the hospital, scans the waybill or tracking barcode, checks that the package is an intact UN3373 Category B triple package with its temperature indicator in range, and logs the arrival time.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations s. 1.39 and CAN/CGSB-43.125 packaging for UN3373 Biological Substance, Category B

evidence.note: Category B packaging rules (tdg_regs); TDG-certified couriers and climate-controlled transport (dyn_logistics); triple packaging (uidl_pack). Box-level time spread over about 20 requisitions per box; estimate.

steps.name: Check the box contents against the hospital's manifest
steps.description: The assistant counts specimens and requisitions in each temperature bag and ticks them off the hospital's printed manifest or the electronic manifest that came over the interface, noting any specimen missing from the box or present without a manifest line.

error.defect_description: A missing specimen is not noticed until the hospital asks for the result.

control.basis: ISO 15189 sample receipt requirements (traceable receipt of every sample against its request) as assessed by Accreditation Canada Diagnostics and CAP

next.condition: manifest missing or count does not match

evidence.note: Accredited quality system with specimen acceptability protocols (dyn_licences, acd). The 4 percent discrepancy rate and times are estimates.

steps.name: Sort specimens by temperature and priority
steps.description: The assistant moves frozen specimens straight to a freezer rack, refrigerated ones to the cold rack and ambient ones to the bench, and pulls out anything marked STAT or time-critical so it is accessioned first.

error.defect_description: Frozen specimen left to thaw on the bench.

evidence.note: Transport temperature and stability limits differ by test (arup_vitd). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a missing manifest or a count mismatch
steps.description: A referral coordinator phones the hospital laboratory's send-out bench, asks for the manifest to be faxed or reprinted from the hospital LIS, and confirms whether a missing specimen was sent, left behind or is in another box; the call and outcome are logged in the client record.

next.condition: hospital must look for the specimen or resend the manifest

evidence.note: Clarifications typically take about 10 minutes and longer once specimens are in transit (capt_clarify); share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Look up the order that came over the hospital interface
steps.description: The assistant scans the hospital's specimen barcode; for an interfaced hospital the LIS finds the electronic order sent by the hospital LIS and shows the patient, ordered tests and hospital accession number.

next.condition: paper requisition or manifest from a hospital without an order interface
interfaced hospital but order not found

evidence.note: Bi-directional interfaces with hospital LIS for orders and results (dyn_hospital); hospital laboratories refer work to each other without regional co-ordination (ag2017), so referring hospitals range from large interfaced ones to small ones sending paper. The 70 percent interfaced share is an estimate; smaller hospitals send printed requisitions. Specimens arriving on the evening line haul wait for the next intake shift.

steps.name: Confirm identifiers and tests against the specimen label
steps.description: The assistant checks that the two identifiers on the tube match the electronic order, that the specimen type and container suit each ordered test, and that test codes map to the reference menu; mapping gaps between the hospital's codes and the laboratory's codes are flagged.

error.defect_description: Mismatch between label and order missed.

control.basis: Two-identifier patient and specimen identification required by ISO 15189 and the CAP Laboratory General checklist

next.condition: identifier, specimen type or test code discrepancy

evidence.note: Two identifiers matching the requisition (uidl_pack); send-out ordering errors are common despite computerised ordering (psnet_sendout). The 6 percent discrepancy rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Trace an interface order that did not arrive
steps.description: A referral coordinator searches the interface engine's message log for the hospital accession number, asks the hospital to resend the order message if it failed, or obtains a printed requisition to enter manually.

evidence.note: Common practice with HL7 order interfaces; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Enter the order from the paper requisition
steps.description: The assistant keys the hospital client code, patient identifiers, hospital accession number, ordering physician and each test into the LIS, choosing the reference test code that matches the hospital's description, and scans the requisition image.

error.defect_description: Wrong test code chosen or identifier mistyped.

evidence.note: Many order forms lack test codes (only 43 percent had them, capt_clarify) and send-out orders are error prone (psnet_sendout). Entry time and error rate are estimates.

steps.name: Check the entered order against the requisition
steps.description: The assistant compares the order on screen with the requisition image and the tube labels, correcting any mismatch in identifiers or test codes before the specimen is labelled.

control.basis: Order-entry verification procedure under the laboratory quality management system

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Check each specimen against the acceptance criteria
steps.description: For every test the assistant checks specimen type, volume, container, transport temperature and the time since collection against the test's stability limit, and looks for haemolysis, lipaemia or thawing.

control.basis: Documented specimen acceptance and rejection criteria required by ISO 15189 and the laboratory's specimen acceptability protocol

next.condition: wrong tube, low volume, wrong temperature, too old or haemolysed

evidence.note: Specimen acceptability protocols in the quality system (dyn_licences); test-specific stability and unacceptable conditions (arup_vitd). The 5 percent problem rate is an estimate within the published range of specimen rejection and problem rates.

steps.name: Hold the requisition and log the problem
steps.description: The assistant puts the affected tests on hold in the LIS with a problem code, moves the specimen to the hold rack at the right temperature and records a nonconformance with the hospital client code.

control.basis: ISO 15189 control of nonconforming work: deviations are recorded and evaluated

evidence.note: Corrective and preventive action and nonconformance recording in the quality system (dyn_licences). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Label and aliquot for the reference benches
steps.description: The assistant prints the laboratory accession labels, labels the primary tube or pours and labels aliquots when several benches or a send-out need the same specimen, and places them in the bench racks at the required temperature.

error.defect_description: Aliquot labelled with the wrong accession.

control.basis: Labelling and traceability of primary samples and aliquots under ISO 15189

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Charge technologist decides on the problem specimen
steps.description: The charge technologist reviews the problem, the test's requirements and whether the specimen can be replaced, and decides to accept it with a qualifying comment, ask the hospital to correct identification or send a new specimen, or reject the test.

error.defect_description: Specimen accepted that should have been rejected.

control.basis: ISO 15189: acceptance of a compromised sample is authorised by competent staff and the report carries a disclaimer

next.condition: needs the hospital to correct or resend

evidence.note: Nonconforming specimens are rejected or returned for correction (uidl_pack). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Call the hospital laboratory to resolve the discrepancy
steps.description: The referral coordinator phones the hospital's send-out bench, explains the problem, asks for a signed identification correction form, the missing information or a new specimen, and records the call in the client record and the LIS hold comment.

evidence.note: Median clarification time 10 minutes; often more than 30 minutes once the specimen is drawn (capt_clarify). Queue time is an estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the hospital to correct the information or resend
steps.description: The hospital laboratory looks up its own records, faxes a correction or completes identification forms, or arranges a recollection and a new shipment.
outputs: correction, new specimen or no reply

next.condition: cannot be corrected; new specimen needed

evidence.note: Some unclear orders are abandoned (about one per thousand, capt_clarify). Wait and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Route the specimen to its testing destination
steps.description: The LIS routing and the assistant's check send each labelled specimen to the right place: the reference chemistry, endocrinology or toxicology bench, the molecular pathology laboratory for tissue tests, or the send-out bench for tests not done in-house.

error.defect_description: Specimen sent to the wrong bench.

next.condition: tissue or block for IHC or molecular tests

evidence.note: Menu of more than 2,000 tests across nine laboratories (dyn_hospital). Destination shares follow the organisation file's volumes for reference testing, send-outs and molecular pathology.

steps.name: Prepare the send-out request
steps.description: The assistant creates the send-out order for the outside laboratory, prints its requisition or manifest line, and places the specimen in the send-out rack for packing on the next scheduled shipment.

error.defect_description: Wrong outside test code or missing information.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations: Category B packaging and marking for onward shipment

evidence.note: Send-out ordering is error prone (psnet_sendout); onward shipment follows Category B rules (tdg_regs). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Hand tissue blocks to molecular pathology
steps.description: The assistant logs the blocks or slides and their pathology report into the molecular pathology queue and walks or sends them with the paperwork to the molecular and cellular pathology laboratory.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Contain and document a damaged or warm package
steps.description: The assistant moves a leaking or broken package to the biosafety cabinet, salvages intact tubes, disinfects, records which specimens are lost or compromised and logs a transport nonconformance for the courier and the hospital.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations and laboratory biosafety procedures for spills of Category B substances

evidence.note: Category B transport rules (tdg_regs). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the hospital to locate the specimen or resend the manifest
steps.description: The hospital laboratory checks its send-out log, finds the missing specimen or manifest and sends it on the next courier or faxes the paperwork.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Reject the test and notify the hospital
steps.description: The assistant cancels the affected test in the LIS with the rejection reason, which flows to the hospital as a cancelled result asking for a new specimen, and the coordinator phones the hospital when the specimen was irreplaceable or urgent.

control.basis: ISO 15189: rejected samples are recorded and the requester is informed

evidence.note: Noncompliant specimens may be rejected and the test not performed (uidl_pack). Times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Manifest missing or count mismatch
exceptions.description: The box does not match its manifest; the coordinator calls the hospital and the specimen waits if the hospital must search or resend.

exceptions.name: Interface order not received
exceptions.description: An interfaced hospital's order message failed; the coordinator asks for a resend or a paper copy.

exceptions.name: Identifier or test code discrepancy
exceptions.description: Label and order disagree or a hospital test description does not map to the reference menu; the requisition is held and the hospital called.

exceptions.name: Unsuitable specimen
exceptions.description: Wrong tube, low volume, wrong temperature, beyond stability or haemolysed; accepted with a comment, corrected, or rejected.

exceptions.name: Damaged package
exceptions.description: A leaking or broken box is contained and the salvageable specimens processed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from arrival at reference receiving to the specimen reaching its bench, molecular queue or send-out rack (0.15 days is about 3.6 hours)
benchmarks.population: Hospital referral requisitions at a large reference laboratory

evidence.note: No published intake cycle time found. Estimate: same shift for clean interfaced referrals; holds that need the hospital (median clarification 10 minutes of work but hours to days of waiting, capt_clarify) and evening arrivals form the tail.

benchmarks.population: CAP Q-Probes participants, small to medium hospitals

benchmarks.unit: minutes (median) to clarify an unclear order

pain_points.description: Paper requisitions describe tests in the hospital's own words, so assistants must find the matching reference test code, and the wrong choice is a common source of error.

evidence.note: Only 43 percent of order forms carry test codes (capt_clarify); send-out ordering errors are common (psnet_sendout).

pain_points.description: Holds that need the hospital to correct an identifier or resend a specimen wait hours to days and take coordinator time on the phone.

evidence.note: Return for correction delays testing (uidl_pack); clarification takes about 10 minutes of work and often over 30 (capt_clarify).

pain_points.description: Interface orders that fail silently leave specimens without orders until someone searches the message log.

evidence.note: Common experience with HL7 order interfaces; estimate.

pain_points.description: Line hauls arrive in waves late in the day, so specimens queue for intake and frozen or time-limited specimens compete for attention.

evidence.note: Estimate based on courier schedules in the organisation's logistics workflow.

sources.title: Hospital solutions
sources.supports: More than 2,000 tests and test combinations, nine Canadian laboratories, more than 60 pathologists, testing for more than 500 teaching and community hospitals; bi-directional interfaces with hospital LIS for orders and results; logistics team for time-sensitive shipments.

sources.title: The model laboratory Logistics
sources.supports: Climate-controlled transport of specimens; all staff hold Transportation of Dangerous Goods certification; Ontario Laboratory Accreditation quality metrics; 24/7 dispatch; secure web-based order and tracking system.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: Brampton, London, Ottawa and Peterborough laboratories accredited to ISO 15189 by Accreditation Canada and licensed by the Ontario ministry; CAP accreditation; quality system includes document control, corrective and preventive action, internal audits, management review, EQA, training and competency, and specimen acceptability protocols.

sources.title: Accreditation Canada Diagnostics
sources.supports: Assesses medical laboratories and specimen collection against ISO 15189 Plus requirements, with an external evaluation at the 2-year mark.

sources.title: Packaging and shipping guidelines
sources.supports: A reference laboratory requires each specimen to carry two identifiers that match the patient information on the requisition; noncompliance may lead to specimen rejection (test not performed) or return for correction, which delays testing; triple packaging with absorbent material, 500 mL maximum per primary container.

sources.title: Labs' problem child: the difficult test order (Q-Probes, Monitoring of outpatient orders requiring clarification)
sources.supports: A median of 1.8 percent of outpatient test orders required clarification; only 43 percent of order forms contained test codes; median clarification time was 10 minutes and often over 30 minutes after the specimen was drawn; orders were abandoned about once per thousand; in 6 percent of unresolved cases staff guessed the intended order; send-out tests were overrepresented among unclear orders.

sources.title: Accuracy of send-out test ordering: a College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of ordering accuracy in 97 clinical laboratories (Valenstein, Walsh, Stankovic, Arch Pathol Lab Med 2008)
sources.supports: Errors in ordering send-out tests sent to specialised regional laboratories were common despite computerised ordering systems (97 laboratories).

sources.title: Vitamin D, 25-hydroxy (test 0080379)
sources.supports: Reference test specimen requirements: 1 mL serum in a transport tube, refrigerated transport; unacceptable: EDTA plasma, grossly haemolysed or lipaemic; stability after separation ambient 72 hours, refrigerated 1 week, frozen 6 months; reported within 24 hours.

sources.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (SOR/2001-286), full text
sources.supports: Section 1.39 sets the conditions for transporting UN3373 Biological Substance, Category B, including a means of containment that meets CGSB-43.125 packaging and the Category B mark.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Hospital laboratories perform tests on behalf of other hospitals and charge them inconsistent prices; hospital laboratory services were not regionally co-ordinated.

sources.title: Wages: Medical laboratory technical assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 26.25, high 36.00 dollars (2023-2024).

assumptions: The case is one hospital referral requisition and starts when its box reaches reference receiving; transport belongs to lg-route-pickup. Referrals from distant hospitals that come by overnight carrier follow the same steps.
About 70 percent of referrals arrive with an electronic order over a hospital LIS interface and 27 percent with a printed requisition or manifest; these shares are estimates.
Box-level work (signing in, checking the package) is spread over about 20 requisitions per box.
Destination shares (86 percent reference benches, 11 percent send-out, 3 percent molecular pathology) are set to match the organisation file's volumes for those processes.
Referral coordinators (5 FTE here) also serve result delivery and send-out tracking, so their remaining headcount is shared with those workflows.
The hospital laboratories' own time is counted as waiting only.

Hands-on time times volume implies about 29 FTE against about 21 stated. The organisation file's 25 referral lab assistants (10 already claimed by reference testing) look low for 50,000 referral requisitions a month plus send-outs; either the referral volume (100 requisitions per hospital a month) is high or the role headcount is low. Stated FTE are capped at what the org file leaves.
Hospital laboratories also refer work to each other at inconsistent prices (ag2017), which is why referral clients include both large interfaced hospitals and small ones sending paper.
